lines: #Everybody wants to get rich *quick.*
That's exactly why so few people get rich at *all.*
#They chase the next big *thing.*
The tip from a stranger. The video promising a *fortune.*
They jump in. They panic. They jump *out.*
And they start again from *zero.*
#Real wealth is *slow.*
So slow it feels like nothing is *happening.*
Month after month. Year after *year.*
And then one day, you look up, and it's *there.*
#Money rewards *patience* more than intelligence.
The ones who win aren't always the *smartest.*
They're the ones who stayed in the game the *longest.*
#So be suspicious of anything that promises you'll be rich *fast.*
If it sounds too good to be true, it almost always *is.*
Build slowly. Learn *constantly.*
Spend less than you earn, and keep doing it for *years.*
It's not exciting. It won't make a great *story.*
#But it works.
Boring money is the money that *stays.*
Let other people chase the *shortcut.*
You just keep *walking.*
end: Save this for when you're tempted by a shortcut.
